financial_trends.evidence: Revenue increased continuously across the three quarters from 70,694 Cr in Q4 FY26 to 72,275 Cr (+2.24% QoQ) in Q1 FY27 and 73,188 Cr (+1.26% QoQ) in Q2 FY27, with YoY growth standing at 11.23% in Q2 FY27.

Operating margin contracted 130 bps from 25.26% in Q4 FY26 to 23.96% in Q1 FY27 due to wage hikes and stepped-up investments, and remained compressed at 23.98% (+2 bps QoQ) in Q2 FY27, well below the historical 25%+ levels.
Net profit rose from 13,702 Cr in Q4 FY26 to 13,849 Cr in Q1 FY27 (+1.07% QoQ) and 13,884 Cr in Q2 FY27 (+0.25% QoQ), maintaining steady net margins near 19%.

management_outlook.summary: Management maintains a cautiously optimistic outlook. They express confidence in medium-term growth driven by pent-up demand, mega deal wins (including an $800M transformation deal with SKF), and rapid AI adoption ($2.3B+ annualized AI revenue). However, management acknowledges near-term margin friction from annual wage increments, stepped-up SG&A investments, ~50 bps acquisition dilution from MHP, and standard Q3 seasonal furloughs.

key_quotes.text: Stepping into FY27, the immediate headwinds would be the annual increments which we have talked about. And also, as you rightly mentioned, we'll continue our focus on the build, acquire and partner framework and investments around that would be part of it... Overall, we'd want to balance it and keep margins within a tighter reach. We'd like to move towards 26%, but on a longer-term basis.
Usually, we take a big headwind upfront in Q1, and we inch up through the quarter. We want to exit at 25% plus and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later.

Looking ahead into the second half, we anticipate a few headwinds. The acquisition-related dilution, particularly in MHP, is likely to impact by about 50 basis points depending on the timing of closure and when the integration starts. The normal furlough seasonality and our continued ecosystem investments would be our headwinds.
And in Q3, so far from what we are seeing, the furlough will be very similar to the previous years. We don't see any major change.

risks.title: Q3 Furlough Seasonality
risks.detail: Q3 is subject to typical seasonal client furloughs, which management noted will be consistent with past years.

risks.title: MHP Acquisition Margin Dilution
risks.detail: The upcoming integration of MHP is projected to dilute operating margin by approximately 50 basis points in H2 FY27.

risks.title: Geopolitical & Discretionary Spend Caution
risks.detail: Persistent macroeconomic uncertainty, inflation, and tariff pressures are leading clients in Consumer Business and Auto to defer discretionary tech spend.

risks.title: SG&A and Ecosystem Investment Costs
risks.detail: Investments under the Build-Partner-Acquire strategy (including OpenAI and ServiceNow ecosystem partnerships) create ongoing SG&A pressure.

opportunities.title: AI and Agentic Transformation Traction
opportunities.detail: Enterprise adoption of generative AI, agentic AI, and cloud modernization is accelerating across sectors, with TCS annualized AI revenues surpassing $2.3 billion.

opportunities.title: Large Deal Wins & Solid Pipeline
opportunities.detail: TCS secured major deal bookings including an $800M transformation deal with SKF and mega deals with Marks & Spencer, a UK telecom operator, and a US healthcare retailer.

opportunities.title: Pent-up Technology Backlog
opportunities.detail: Management identified significant pent-up technology demand among clients that deferred projects in Q1 FY27, expected to drive revenue recovery over the coming quarters.

opportunities.title: MHP Acquisition & High-Growth Sectors
opportunities.detail: The acquisition of MHP enhances TCS's capabilities in automotive and smart manufacturing, establishing an AI Centre of Excellence for mobility.

forecast.revenue_outlook: Revenue growth in Q3 FY27 is expected to be modest or flat-to-slightly positive on a sequential basis. Growth will be supported by AI-led enterprise transformations and large deal execution, but dampened by typical Q3 client furloughs and persistent spending caution in retail and consumer business verticals.
forecast.margin_outlook: Operating margin in Q3 FY27 is expected to face downward pressure or remain range-bound (around 23.5%–24.0%). Primary margin headwinds include normal Q3 seasonal furloughs, ~50 bps dilution from the MHP acquisition, and elevated ecosystem/SG&A investments, partially cushioned by currency tailwinds and operating efficiency levers.
forecast.overall_outlook: TCS is positioned for steady top-line execution in Q3 FY27, backed by strong AI transformation traction ($2.3B+ annualized AI revenues) and solid deal bookings. However, revenue growth will be tempered by standard third-quarter seasonal furloughs and discretionary spending caution. Margins will remain under pressure due to the MHP acquisition integration (~50 bps dilution) and furlough impact, keeping EBIT margin below management's medium-term 25% target in the near term.
